name: east-west scrap fence section: two rails of folded corrugated sheet metal on a wooden post, rail tops seen from above, tiles into a line
label: wasteland_ruins/fence-h

answer.evidence: Each rail has a top band of 3 rows (rows 3-5 and 10-12). A light edge row opens the band, and the band ends in a rust front-edge line (rows 6 and 13) followed by a 1-row dark shadow (rows 7 and 14). The rail's own front face is only about 2 rows. The wooden post provides a vertical front face of rows 1-14 (width 5), and its top cap is a 1-row light end at row 0. The rails are horizontal beams that show top faces, so the frame rule is met, but the front face is thin. The 3-row top, edge line and shadow, together with the post's tall front, read as three-quarter, though only weakly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, thin fence tile: two grey corrugated rails on a brown wooden post. The facts support it. It has 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above the hedge (9) and close to the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean toward the material (dark brown beside the post, dark grey-blue beside the metal) rather than being a black sticker line. By eye, the rails show a few lightness steps (highlight, mid, dark, deep) with corrugation ridges and the wood has grain. That is slightly fewer steps than the 5-6 on the references, but it reads as similar craft for such a thin prop and does not look flatter than the bench or the lamp. The candidate is small, so I judged mostly on the measured facts, and the image is too low-resolution to rule out some flatness within the rails.

answer.evidence: Each 16px-wide rail has a light top row (3 or 10), then mid-tone rows of rail top, then a reddish front-edge line (row 6 or 13) and a 1-row dark shadow (row 7 or 14). The post (x=8) has a light top band at rows 0-3, a darker edge line at row 4, and a dark front face at rows 5-14, which is 10 rows. The post's top band is lighter and ends in an edge line. Both major parts show a top surface and a front face, so the object reads as three-quarter, not a flat slab or a pure front elevation. The 3-row rail top is thin but meets the edge-line evidence.

answer.evidence: Each rail is a 16px-wide horizontal part. A 1-row dark shadow follows (row 7 or 14). That makes about 3 rows of top surface per rail. Below the edge line the rail has only the 1-row shadow, so the rails have almost no front face of their own. The vertical wooden post (x 5-9, rows 0-14) supplies the front face. It is a plain vertical strip with a 1-row lighter cap at row 0 and no top surface of its own. The three-quarter reading is borderline because the rails are thin and the post is the only tall front face.
